q: What did the first PAT cycle achieve?
title: PAT cycle I results
short: PAT cycle I ran from 2012-13 to 2014-15 for 478 plants in eight sectors. It targeted 6.686 million tonnes of oil equivalent of energy savings and achieved 8.67, which BEE puts at about 31 million tonnes of CO2 avoided. Over-achievers earned Energy Saving Certificates, or ESCerts, to sell.
audience: Energy managers at designated consumers and plants preparing for CCTS targets

p: 478 designated consumers in aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali, fertiliser, iron and steel, pulp and paper, thermal power and textiles. Each got a specific energy consumption target based on how efficient it already was, so efficient plants got smaller cuts.

ul: Target: 6.686 MTOE, about 4.05% of the sectors' energy use
ESCerts issued: about 38.25 lakh to 306 plants
Plants told to buy ESCerts for shortfalls: 110, for about 14.25 lakh

p: The same plants and sectors form the core of the CCTS compliance market. Plants that kept clean PAT records already know how to report production, energy and baselines in the form a regulator checks.

senseible: Senseible turns fuel and electricity invoices into monthly energy and emission records per site, the raw material for tracking specific energy consumption against a target.
